note: DRAFT LIBRARY. Every step is paraphrased from an official government page (source_url; US federal and state sites, and since version 4 also official Australian, UK, EU, New Zealand and Canadian sites), and the supporting quote was checked word for word against that page (versions 1-3 on 2026-11-07, version 4 on 2026-11-23). Version 4 adds first aid and more emergencies by the maintainer's decision after the first tester chats. Not yet reviewed by qualified experts: not for real emergencies. Process: content/README.md.

guides.title: Lost: stay put or move?
guides.summary: Deciding whether to stay where you are or try to move.

steps.text: Stop. Take a moment to calmly look at your situation.
steps.quote: Take a moment to calmly assess your situation

steps.text: If you have a map, compass or GPS, or can see landmarks, use them to try to work out where you are.
steps.quote: Use your map, compass, handheld GPS, or visible landmarks to try to find your location

steps.text: If it's safe, retrace your steps to get back to the route you planned.
steps.quote: If it is safe to do so, retrace your steps to get back on your planned route

steps.text: If you can't safely find your way back, stay where you are.
steps.quote: Stay put

steps.text: Changing location will make it hard for searchers to find you. Move only if there is an immediate threat to life.
steps.quote: Changing location will make it difficult for authorities to find you. Move only if there is an immediate threat to life

guides.title: Help rescuers find you
guides.summary: Making yourself easy to see and hear.

steps.text: If you have a whistle, blow it often. It helps people find you and saves the energy you'd use yelling.
steps.quote: Blowing a whistle helps people find you and saves your energy from yelling.

steps.text: If you have a flashlight, flash SOS: three quick flashes, three slow, then three quick.
steps.quote: Flash the SOS pattern: Three times quickly, three times slowly, three times quickly.

steps.text: If you have a mirror, flash it toward planes or helicopters flying nearby.
steps.quote: This can alert planes and helicopters flying in the area

steps.text: Lay out brightly colored clothing in an open clearing where searchers can see it.
steps.quote: Lay out brightly-colored clothing in a forest clearing.

guides.title: Cold, wet or bad weather
guides.summary: Staying protected from cold, wind, rain and snow.

steps.text: Find shelter. Try to stay dry and cover all exposed skin.
steps.quote: Find Shelter: Try to stay dry and cover all exposed body parts.

steps.text: If there's no shelter, build a lean-to or windbreak to block the wind.
steps.quote: Build a lean-to, windbreak or snow cave for protection from the wind.

steps.text: If you have a wind- or waterproof jacket, wear it to keep out wind, rain and wet snow.
steps.quote: a wind and waterproof jacket will keep out wind, rain and wet snow

steps.text: Wool or synthetic clothing is better than cotton. Cotton soaks up water and won't keep you warm when it's wet.
steps.quote: Choose clothing made of wool or synthetic material over cotton. Cotton absorbs moisture easily and won’t keep you warm if it gets wet.

steps.text: Keep your feet as dry as you can.
steps.quote: Keep feet dry with wool socks, gaiters, and insulated boots.

guides.title: Heat and sun
guides.summary: Staying protected from heat and strong sun.

steps.text: Rest in the shade.
steps.quote: Set up your tent in the shade

steps.text: If you have a wide-brimmed hat, wear it to shield your face and neck from the sun.
steps.quote: Wear a wide brim sun hat to shield your face and neck from the sun as much as possible

steps.text: Avoid hard activity during the hottest part of the day if you can.
steps.quote: Avoid high-energy activities or outdoor work during midday heat if possible.

steps.text: Drink plenty of water, even if you don't feel thirsty.
steps.quote: Whether you feel thirsty or not, drink plenty of water

steps.text: The temperature inside a parked vehicle can rapidly rise to a dangerous level for children, pets and even adults.
steps.quote: the temperature inside a parked vehicle can rapidly rise to a dangerous level for children, pets and even adults.

guides.title: Water
guides.summary: Thinking about drinking water.

steps.text: Don't ration your drinking water unless authorities tell you to. Drink what you need today and try to find more for tomorrow.
steps.quote: Never ration drinking water unless ordered to do so by authorities. Drink the amount you need today and try to find more for tomorrow.

steps.text: Streams, rivers and other moving water can be sources of water.
steps.quote: Streams, rivers, and other moving bodies of water

steps.text: Water from outdoor sources must be treated to kill germs before you drink it.
steps.quote: Water from sources outside the home must be treated to kill harmful germs as described in Make Water Safe in an Emergency.

steps.text: If the water might have fuel or chemicals in it, don't drink it. Boiling won't make it safe.
steps.quote: If you suspect or know the water is contaminated with toxic chemicals or fuels, it cannot be made safe and you should not drink or bathe in this water.

steps.text: If the water is cloudy, first filter it through a clean cloth, paper towel or coffee filter.
steps.quote: If the water is cloudy, first filter it through a clean cloth, paper towel, or coffee filter.

steps.text: Bring clear water to a rolling boil for 1 minute. Above 6,500 feet, boil it for 3 minutes.
steps.quote: Bring clear water to a rolling boil for 1 minute (at elevations above 6,500 feet, boil for 3 minutes).

steps.text: Do not drink seawater. Drinking seawater can be deadly to humans.
steps.quote: Drinking seawater can be deadly to humans.

steps.text: Melt snow before drinking it. Eating unmelted snow will lower your body temperature.
steps.quote: Melt Snow for Drinking Water: Eating unmelted snow will lower your body temperature.

guides.title: Make your phone battery last
guides.summary: Saving battery so your phone works when it matters.

steps.text: Use your phone as little as possible to save battery.
steps.quote: If the power goes out save battery power by minimizing device use.

steps.text: Turn on low power mode, or airplane mode, to save energy.
steps.quote: Change the settings on your phone to low power mode or place it on airplane mode to conserve energy.

steps.text: Dim your screen and turn off apps you don't need.
steps.quote: dimming the brightness of your display screen and disabling certain applications.

steps.text: Keep any calls short and share only vital information.
steps.quote: If you do need to make a call, try to keep it brief and only convey vital information to emergency personnel and family.

steps.text: If you have no signal bars, turning the phone off stops it draining the battery while it searches for signal.
steps.quote: turning your phone off helps prevent the battery from draining as your phone seeks a usable wireless signal.

guides.title: Contact help when you get signal
guides.summary: Reaching emergency services if any connection appears.

steps.text: As soon as you have signal, call 911.
steps.quote: In an emergency, dial 911 from your phone immediately.

steps.text: Call if you can, text if you can't. Some areas accept texts to 911, but a voice call is best.
steps.quote: call 911 if you can and text if you can't

steps.text: Be ready to tell them where you are, as exactly as you can.
steps.quote: The location of the emergency, including the street address

steps.text: Tell them the phone number you're calling from.
steps.quote: The phone number you are calling from

steps.text: Tell them what the emergency is.
steps.quote: The nature of the emergency

steps.text: Don't hang up until the call-taker tells you to.
steps.quote: Do not hang up until the call-taker instructs you to do so.

guides.title: Stranded in a vehicle
guides.summary: Stuck in a car, truck or other vehicle.

steps.text: Stay with your vehicle and try not to panic.
steps.quote: If you should become stranded during a winter storm, stay with your vehicle and do not panic.

steps.text: Before running the engine, make sure the exhaust pipe isn't blocked.
steps.quote: Make sure the exhaust pipe is not blocked.

steps.text: In the cold, run the engine about 10 minutes each hour for warmth, with a window open a little to keep out carbon monoxide.
steps.quote: Run the motor every hour for about ten minutes to maintain warmth, but keep windows open a little to prevent the buildup of carbon monoxide.

steps.text: Make your car easy to see: tie brightly colored cloth to a mirror, door handle or antenna.
steps.quote: Keep the car visible with brightly colored cloths tied to the side view mirrors, door handles, or external antenna.

steps.text: At night, turn on the inside light while the engine is running.
steps.quote: At night, turn on the dome light when running the engine.

steps.text: In snow and wind, if you leave your vehicle you will become disoriented quickly.
steps.quote: If you leave your vehicle, you will become disoriented quickly in wind-driven snow and cold.

steps.text: After snow stops falling, raise the hood to show you need help.
steps.quote: After snow stops falling, raise the hood to indicate you need help.

guides.title: Stay calm and think clearly
guides.summary: Getting through fear and panic.

steps.text: Stay calm and think through your situation.
steps.quote: Stay calm and think through the situation.

steps.text: If you're waiting for help, rest, save your energy and wait patiently.
steps.quote: Wait patiently for help to arrive and conserve your energy

guides.title: Flooding and rising water
guides.summary: Flood water on the road, around you or coming into the car.

steps.text: Do not walk, swim or drive through flood water. Turn around, don't drown.
steps.quote: Do not walk, swim or drive through flood waters. Turn Around, Don’t Drown!

steps.text: Just six inches of moving water can knock you down, and one foot of moving water can sweep a vehicle away.
steps.quote: Remember, just six inches of moving water can knock you down, and one foot of moving water can sweep your vehicle away.

steps.text: Stay off bridges over fast-moving water.
steps.quote: Stay off bridges over fast-moving water.

steps.text: If your car is trapped in rapidly moving water, stay inside it. If water is rising inside the car, get on the roof.
steps.quote: Stay inside your car if it is trapped in rapidly moving water. Get on the roof if water is rising inside the car.

steps.text: Evacuate right away if you are told to.
steps.quote: Evacuate immediately, if told to do so.

guides.title: Wildfire and smoke
guides.summary: Fire, smoke or an evacuation order nearby.

steps.text: If authorities tell you to evacuate, go right away.
steps.quote: Evacuate immediately if authorities tell you to do so.

steps.text: Pay attention to emergency alerts and notifications for information and instructions.
steps.quote: Pay attention to emergency alerts and notifications for information and instructions.

steps.text: If you are trapped, call 911 and give your location. Help may be delayed. Turn on lights to help rescuers find you.
steps.quote: If trapped, call 9-1-1 and give your location, but be aware that emergency response could be delayed or impossible. Turn on lights to help rescuers find you.

guides.title: Lightning and thunderstorms
guides.summary: Thunder or lightning nearby while you are outside.

steps.text: There is no safe place outside when thunderstorms are in the area.
steps.quote: There is no safe place outside when thunderstorms are in the area.

steps.text: Substantial buildings and hard-topped vehicles are safe options. Rain shelters, small sheds, and open vehicles are not safe.
steps.quote: Substantial buildings and hard-topped vehicles are safe options. Rain shelters, small sheds, and open vehicles are not safe.

steps.text: A tent offers no protection from lightning.
steps.quote: Remember, a tent offers NO protection from lighting.

steps.text: Avoid open fields, the top of a hill or a ridge top.
steps.quote: Avoid open fields, the top of a hill or a ridge top.

steps.text: Stay away from tall, isolated trees or other tall objects. If you are in a forest, stay near a lower stand of trees.
steps.quote: Stay away from tall, isolated trees or other tall objects. If you are in a forest, stay near a lower stand of trees.

steps.text: If you are in a group, spread out to avoid the current traveling between group members.
steps.quote: If you are in a group, spread out to avoid the current traveling between group members.

steps.text: Stay away from water, wet items such as ropes, and metal objects such as fences and poles.
steps.quote: Stay away from water, wet items, such as ropes, and metal objects, such as fences and poles.

steps.text: Wait 30 minutes after the last lightning or thunder before going back outside.
steps.quote: Finally, wait 30 minutes after the last lightning or thunder before going back outside.

guides.title: Strong wind and falling trees
guides.summary: High wind, gusts, falling branches or downed power lines.

steps.text: Take shelter in your car if you are not near a sturdy building.
steps.quote: Take shelter in your car if you are not near a sturdy building.

steps.text: If no shelter is available, avoid trees, power lines, and the side of the road.
steps.quote: If no shelter is available avoid trees, power lines, and the side of the road.

steps.text: Power lines that are lying on the ground may be live. Do not go near them.
steps.quote: Keep in mind that power lines that are laying on the ground may be live. Do not go near them!

steps.text: Try to find a place that will block blowing or falling debris.
steps.quote: Try to find a place that will block blowing or falling debris.

steps.text: Tornado: if a tornado is coming, get inside a sturdy building right away.
steps.quote: Seek shelter inside a sturdy building immediately if a tornado is approaching.

steps.text: Tornado: a tent or mobile home is not safe.
steps.quote: Neither is a mobile home or tent.

steps.text: Tornado: being in a vehicle is not safe.
steps.quote: Being in a vehicle during a tornado is not safe.

steps.text: Tornado: if you can't reach a safe shelter, either get down in your car and cover your head, or leave the car and get into a low spot such as a ditch or ravine.
steps.quote: If you are unable to make it to a safe shelter, either get down in your car and cover your head

steps.text: Dust storm while driving: pull your vehicle off the pavement as far as you can.
steps.quote: pull your vehicle off the pavement as far as possible

steps.text: Dust storm while driving: then stop, turn off your lights, set the emergency brake and take your foot off the brake.
steps.quote: stop, turn off lights, set the emergency brake

steps.text: Dust storm: never stop on the part of the road where cars drive.
steps.quote: Never stop on the traveled portion of the roadway.

guides.title: Beach, tides and waves
guides.summary: On a beach or coast with tides, waves or cliffs.

steps.text: Stay farther back from the ocean than you think is necessary.
steps.quote: Stay farther back from the ocean than you think is necessary.

steps.text: Never turn your back on the ocean.
steps.quote: Never turn your back on the ocean.

steps.text: Stay off and well clear of large logs and debris near the surf line or below the high water marks.
steps.quote: Stay off and well clear of large logs and debris fields that are anywhere near the surfline or below the high water marks.

steps.text: Cold water immersion can be dangerous, even deadly.
steps.quote: Cold water immersion can be dangerous, even deadly.

steps.text: Strong winds or storms can significantly raise tides and create hazardous conditions.
steps.quote: Strong winds or storms can significantly elevate tides and create hazardous conditions

steps.text: Stay several meters away from the base of cliffs, and from the edge of clifftops.
steps.quote: you should stay several meters away from the base of the cliffs, as well as from the edge of clifftops.

guides.title: Wild animals nearby
guides.summary: A bear, mountain lion, snake or other wild animal close by.

steps.text: Never approach wildlife. If an animal moves closer to you, back away to keep a safe distance.
steps.quote: If an animal moves closer to you, back away to maintain a safe distance.

steps.text: Bear: talk calmly so the bear knows you are a human and not a prey animal.
steps.quote: Identify yourself by talking calmly so the bear knows you are a human and not a prey animal.

steps.text: Bear: do not run or make any sudden movements.
steps.quote: Do NOT run or make any sudden movements.

steps.text: Bear: pick up small children immediately.
steps.quote: Pick up small children immediately.

steps.text: Bear: do not climb a tree.
steps.quote: Do NOT climb a tree.

steps.text: Mountain lion: do not run from it. Stand and face the animal.
steps.quote: Do not run from a lion. Running may stimulate a mountain lion's instinct to chase. Instead, stand and face the animal.

steps.text: Mountain lion: if you have small children with you, pick them up if possible so that they do not panic and run.
steps.quote: If you have small children with you, pick them up if possible so that they don't panic and run.

steps.text: Mountain lion: do all you can to appear larger. Raise your arms.
steps.quote: Do all you can to appear larger. Raise your arms.

steps.text: Snake: give it plenty of room to leave the area.
steps.quote: The most important thing to remember about snakes is to give them plenty of room to leave an area if encountered.

guides.title: Children and groups
guides.summary: Children, older people or a group with you.

steps.text: Keep children close to you.
steps.quote: Keep children close to you.

steps.text: Watch children closely and never let them run ahead of you.
steps.quote: When hiking with children, watch them closely and never let them run ahead of you.

steps.text: If you are with others in a stranded vehicle, take turns sleeping.
steps.quote: If accompanied by others, take turns sleeping.

steps.text: In heat, children, infants and older adults should stay in the coolest available place.
steps.quote: should stay in the coolest available place, not necessarily indoors.

steps.text: Never leave a child unattended in a vehicle, even with the windows down, even for just a minute.
steps.quote: Never leave a child unattended in a vehicle, even with the windows down, even for just a minute

guides.title: Snake bite
guides.summary: Someone was bitten by a snake.

steps.text: Treat every snake bite as dangerous. It can be hard to tell which snakes are venomous, so don't wait to find out.
steps.quote: All snake bites must be treated as potentially life-threatening

steps.text: Get medical help as soon as you can. Don't wait for symptoms to appear.
steps.quote: Do not wait for symptoms to appear

steps.text: Get away from the snake. Don't try to catch or kill it.
steps.quote: Do not try to catch or kill the snake

steps.text: Keep as still and calm as you can. Lie or sit down with the bitten part in a comfortable, neutral position.
steps.quote: Lay or sit down with the bite in a neutral position of comfort

steps.text: Take off rings, watches and anything tight near the bite before it swells.
steps.quote: Remove rings and watches before swelling starts

steps.text: Don't cut the bite and don't try to suck the venom out.
steps.quote: Do not try to suck out the venom

steps.text: Don't use a tourniquet, ice, or alcohol.
steps.quote: Do not apply a tourniquet

steps.text: Don't drive yourself if someone else can, or if help can come to you.
steps.quote: Do not drive yourself

steps.text: US (CDC): wash the bite with soap and water and cover it with a clean, dry dressing.
steps.quote: Wash the bite with soap and water

steps.text: US (CDC): mark the edge of the swelling and write down the time, so helpers can see if it spreads.
steps.quote: Mark the leading edge of tenderness/swelling on the skin and write the time alongside it

steps.text: Australia: don't wash the bite. Venom left on the skin and clothes can help doctors work out which snake it was.
steps.quote: Do not wash the bite area — venom left on the skin and clothing can help identify the snake

steps.text: Australia: put a firm pressure bandage over the bite, then bandage the whole limb from the fingers or toes upward, and keep it still with a splint.
steps.quote: Apply a pressure bandage

steps.text: If the person stops responding or isn't breathing normally, start CPR if you know how.
steps.quote: Start cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), if the person is unresponsive or not breathing normally

steps.text: Stay with the bitten person.
steps.quote: Stay with the person

guides.title: Broken bone or bad sprain
guides.summary: A possible broken arm, leg, ankle or other bone, and how to splint it.

steps.text: Keep the injured person still and calm.
steps.quote: Keep the person still and calm

steps.text: Don't move someone who may have hurt their neck or back, unless they're in danger where they are.
steps.quote: DO NOT move a person who has a possible spine injury

steps.text: Don't try to straighten the bone or push it back into place. (The only exception: blood flow past the injury looks cut off and no trained help is near.)
steps.quote: DO NOT attempt to straighten a bone or change its position unless blood circulation appears hampered and no medically trained personnel are nearby

steps.text: If the skin is broken, cover the wound with a clean, dry cloth. If it keeps bleeding, press firmly on it. Don't use a tourniquet unless the bleeding is life-threatening.
steps.quote: apply direct pressure to the site of bleeding

steps.text: To make a splint, use something stiff, like a rolled-up newspaper or strips of wood, and tie it so the joints above and below the break can't move.
steps.quote: Possible splints include a rolled up newspaper or strips of wood. Immobilize the area both above and below the injured bone

steps.text: For an arm, a towel can work as a sling.
steps.quote: use a towel as a sling to support the affected arm

steps.text: Take off rings, watches and bracelets on that limb before it swells.
steps.quote: remove any jewellery such as rings or watches

steps.text: Check the skin past the injury, like fingers or toes. If it's pale, blue, cold or numb, blood flow may be cut off, so get help fast.
steps.quote: Check the person's blood circulation

steps.text: Try not to move a leg that may be broken, and don't put weight on it.
steps.quote: avoid moving your leg or putting weight on it

guides.title: Emergency numbers outside the US
guides.summary: Which number to call in Australia, the UK, Europe, New Zealand and Canada.

steps.text: Australia: call Triple Zero (000).
steps.quote: Call Triple Zero (000) in an emergency

steps.text: Australia: on a mobile you can also dial 112. It reaches the same 000 service.
steps.quote: which will direct you to the same Triple Zero (000) service

steps.text: Australia: you can't text 000, so call when you get any signal.
steps.quote: You cannot contact Triple Zero (000) by SMS

steps.text: UK: call 999.
steps.quote: Call 999

steps.text: Europe: call 112. It works free across the EU, and on most mobile networks worldwide.
steps.quote: 112 is the European emergency phone number, available everywhere in the EU, free of charge

steps.text: New Zealand: call 111 and ask for the service you need.
steps.quote: Call 111 and ask for Police

steps.text: Canada: call 911 for police, fire or ambulance.
steps.quote: Call 911 for police, fire or ambulance

guides.title: Bad bleeding
guides.summary: A cut or wound that is bleeding a lot.

steps.text: Press hard right on the wound with a clean cloth, a piece of clothing, or your hand if there's nothing else.
steps.quote: Put pressure directly on an external wound with a sterile bandage, clean cloth, or even a piece of clothing

steps.text: Keep pressing until the bleeding stops. Don't lift the cloth to check.
steps.quote: Do not peek to see if the bleeding has stopped

steps.text: If blood soaks through, don't take the cloth off. Put another one on top and keep pressing.
steps.quote: Simply place another cloth over the first one

steps.text: Lay the person down, and raise the bleeding part if you can.
steps.quote: Lay the person down

steps.text: If something is stuck in the wound, like a stick or knife, leave it in. Pad around it and hold it in place.
steps.quote: Do not remove an object such as a knife, stick, or arrow that is stuck in the body

steps.text: Only if pressure hasn't stopped life-threatening bleeding from an arm or leg: tie a tourniquet 2 to 3 inches (5 to 7 cm) above the wound, not on a joint.
steps.quote: The tourniquet should be applied to the limb 2 to 3 in (5 to 7.7 cm) above the bleeding wound

steps.text: To make a tourniquet: wrap a wide strip of cloth around the limb several times, tie a knot, put a stick on the knot, tie it again, and twist the stick until the bleeding stops. Then fix the stick in place.
steps.quote: Twist the stick until the bandage is tight enough to stop the bleeding and then secure it in place

steps.text: Write down or remember the time you put the tourniquet on, and tell rescuers.
steps.quote: always write down the time when the tourniquet was applied

steps.text: For heavy bleeding, also watch for shock: lay them flat, raise their feet about 12 inches (30 cm), and keep them warm with a coat or blanket. Don't raise the feet if the head, neck, back or legs are hurt.
steps.quote: raise the feet about 12 inches (in) or 30 centimeters (cm), and cover the person with a coat or blanket

guides.title: Burns
guides.summary: A burn from fire, hot water, steam or electricity.

steps.text: If someone's clothes are on fire: stop, drop and roll. Wrap them in a thick coat or blanket to put out the flames.
steps.quote: If someone is on fire, tell the person to stop, drop, and roll

steps.text: If you're not sure how bad the burn is, treat it as a serious one and get help.
steps.quote: If you are not sure, treat it as a major burn

steps.text: For a small burn with unbroken skin, run cool (not icy) water over it for at least 5 minutes, up to 30.
steps.quote: Keep the area under water for at least 5 to 30 minutes

steps.text: Cover the burn loosely with a clean, dry cloth or bandage.
steps.quote: cover it with a dry, sterile bandage or clean dressing

steps.text: Don't put butter, oil, ice, creams or home remedies on a serious burn.
steps.quote: Do not apply oil, butter, ice, medicines, cream, oil spray, or any household remedy to a severe burn

steps.text: Don't pop blisters, and don't pull off clothing that's stuck to the burn.
steps.quote: Do not remove clothing that is stuck to the skin

steps.text: Don't put a large, serious burn in cold water. It can cause shock.
steps.quote: Do not place a severe burn in cold water

steps.text: If the burn came from electricity, don't touch the person until they're away from the power. Use something that isn't metal to move them off the wire.
steps.quote: do not touch the victim directly

guides.title: Choking
guides.summary: Someone can't breathe because something is stuck in their throat.

steps.text: Ask: "Are you choking? Can you speak?" If they're coughing hard and can talk, let them keep coughing.
steps.quote: Encourage the person to keep coughing to dislodge the object

steps.text: If they can't speak or breathe, give 5 back blows, then 5 abdominal thrusts, and repeat until it comes out.
steps.quote: You should perform repeated cycles of 5 back blows followed by 5 abdominal thrusts

steps.text: Back blows: stand behind them, lean them forward, and hit firmly between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.
steps.quote: Use the heel of your other hand to deliver a firm blow between the person's shoulder blades

steps.text: Abdominal thrusts: wrap your arms around their waist, put your fist just above the belly button, grab it with your other hand, and pull in and up hard.
steps.quote: Make a quick, upward and inward thrust with your fist

steps.text: If the person is pregnant or very large, push on the middle of the breastbone instead of the belly.
steps.quote: In pregnant or obese people, chest thrusts should be done instead of abdominal thrusts

steps.text: If they pass out, lay them on a firm surface, shout for help, and start CPR. Look in the mouth for the object before each breath.
steps.quote: Check for an object in the mouth before giving breaths

steps.text: Don't reach into the throat to grab something stuck there. Only take it out if you can see it loose in the mouth.
steps.quote: If the object is lodged in the person's throat, do not try to grasp it

guides.title: Not breathing: CPR
guides.summary: Someone has collapsed and isn't responding or breathing normally.

steps.text: Tap or gently shake them and shout "Are you OK?"
steps.quote: Shake or tap the person gently

steps.text: If they don't respond, shout for help and get someone to call emergency services. If you're alone, call yourself if you have any signal.
steps.quote: Shout for help and send someone to call 911 or the local emergency number

steps.text: Lay them on their back on a firm, flat surface.
steps.quote: Place the person on a firm, flat surface, if possible

steps.text: Put the heel of one hand in the center of the chest, between the nipples, with your other hand on top.
steps.quote: Place the heel of one hand in the center of the person

steps.text: With straight arms, push down hard and fast about 2 inches (5 cm), 30 times. Let the chest come all the way back up each time.
steps.quote: Press down about 2 inches (5 centimeters) into the chest

steps.text: Then tilt the head back, lift the chin, pinch the nose, and give 2 breaths that make the chest rise.
steps.quote: Give 2 rescue breaths

steps.text: Keep going: 30 pushes, then 2 breaths, about 100 to 120 pushes a minute, until they recover or help arrives.
steps.quote: Do 100 to 120 compressions per minute

steps.text: If there's an AED (heart defibrillator) nearby, use it as soon as you can.
steps.quote: If an AED is available, use it as soon as possible

steps.text: If they start breathing again, roll them onto their side (the recovery position).
steps.quote: place them in the recovery position

guides.title: Severe allergic reaction
guides.summary: Swelling, trouble breathing or a hoarse voice after a sting, food or medicine.

steps.text: This is an emergency. Get help right away.
steps.quote: Anaphylaxis is an emergency condition that needs medical attention right away

steps.text: If they have an epinephrine injector (like an EpiPen), help them use it right away.
steps.quote: An epinephrine injector or intranasal epinephrine should be used immediately if it is available

steps.text: A very hoarse or whispery voice, or rough noises when breathing in, are warning signs that the throat is swelling.
steps.quote: A warning sign of dangerous throat swelling is a very hoarse or whispered voice

steps.text: If it was a bee sting, scrape the stinger off with a fingernail or card. Don't squeeze it with tweezers.
steps.quote: Squeezing the stinger will release more venom

steps.text: Don't give anything by mouth if they're having trouble breathing, and don't put a pillow under their head.
steps.quote: Do not give the person anything by mouth if they are having trouble breathing

steps.text: If they're not hurt and not vomiting, lay them flat, raise their feet about 12 inches (30 cm), and keep them warm.
steps.quote: raise the person's feet about 12 inches (in) or 30 centimeters (cm), and cover the person with a coat or blanket

steps.text: If they stop breathing, start CPR.
steps.quote: If necessary, begin rescue breathing and CPR

guides.title: Head injury
guides.summary: A hit to the head, a fall, or someone knocked out.

steps.text: Get help fast if they're very sleepy, confused, have a bad headache, vomit more than once, have a seizure, can't move an arm or leg, or were knocked out even briefly.
steps.quote: Loses consciousness, even briefly

steps.text: If they're unconscious but breathing, treat it as a neck injury too: hold their head still, in line with the body.
steps.quote: Keep the head in line with the spine and prevent movement

steps.text: Stop bleeding by pressing a clean cloth on it, unless the skull might be broken. Then just cover it, without pressing.
steps.quote: If you suspect a skull fracture, do not apply direct pressure to the bleeding site

steps.text: If they start to vomit, roll their head, neck and body together onto their side, keeping the head still.
steps.quote: roll the person's head, neck, and body as one unit

steps.text: Don't move them unless you have to, and don't shake someone who seems dazed.
steps.quote: Do not shake the person if they seem dazed

steps.text: Don't take off a helmet if the head injury might be serious.
steps.quote: Do not remove a helmet if you suspect a serious head injury

steps.text: Keep watching them. Signs of a head injury can show up later.
steps.quote: watch for symptoms of a head injury, which can show up later

guides.title: Seizure
guides.summary: Someone is shaking, jerking or has collapsed with a seizure.

steps.text: Stay calm and stay with them.
steps.quote: Stay with the person

steps.text: Ease them to the ground and move away anything that could hurt them.
steps.quote: Ease them to the ground if they appear to be falling

steps.text: Turn them gently onto one side, mouth pointing down, to keep the airway clear.
steps.quote: Turn them gently onto one side with their mouth pointing to the ground

steps.text: Put something soft under their head, take off glasses, and loosen anything tight around the neck.
steps.quote: Loosen anything around the neck that could block breathing

steps.text: Don't hold them down, and don't put anything in their mouth.
steps.quote: Don't put anything in their mouth

steps.text: Time it. Get emergency help if it lasts more than 5 minutes, another one follows, they're hurt, it happens in water, or they have trouble breathing or waking up.
steps.quote: The seizure lasts longer than 5 minutes

steps.text: Afterward, help them sit somewhere safe, and tell them calmly what happened.
steps.quote: Once they are alert, comfort them and explain what happened

guides.title: Heart attack signs
guides.summary: Chest pain or pressure, maybe with sweating, short breath or arm or jaw pain.

steps.text: Signs of a heart attack: chest pain or pressure that lasts more than a few minutes or comes back, pain in the jaw, neck, back, arm or shoulder, shortness of breath, feeling faint, or a cold sweat.
steps.quote: Most heart attacks involve discomfort in the center or left side of the chest that lasts for more than a few minutes or that goes away and comes back

steps.text: Get emergency help right away. The sooner it's treated, the less damage to the heart.
steps.quote: The more time that passes without treatment to restore blood flow, the greater the damage to the heart muscle

steps.text: If they collapse and stop breathing normally, start CPR, and use an AED if there is one.
steps.quote: In some cases, a heart attack requires cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) or an electrical shock (defibrillation) to the heart

guides.title: Stroke signs
guides.summary: A drooping face, a weak arm, slurred speech, or sudden trouble seeing or walking.

steps.text: Check quickly. Face: ask them to smile. Does one side droop? Arms: ask them to raise both. Does one drift down? Speech: ask them to repeat a simple phrase. Is it slurred or strange?
steps.quote: Ask the person to smile. Does one side of the face droop?

steps.text: Other sudden signs: trouble walking or with balance, trouble seeing, numbness on one side, confusion, or a severe headache.
steps.quote: Sudden numbness or weakness in the face, arm, or leg, especially on one side of the body

steps.text: If you see any of these, get emergency help right away. Every minute counts.
steps.quote: During a stroke, every minute counts

steps.text: Write down or remember the time the signs started. Doctors need it.
steps.quote: Note the time when any symptoms first appear

steps.text: Where an ambulance can come, call one rather than driving: crews start treatment on the way.
steps.quote: Call 9-1-1 for an ambulance so that medical personnel can begin life-saving treatment on the way

guides.title: Heat stroke and heat exhaustion
guides.summary: Someone is overheating: confused, dizzy, very hot, or has stopped sweating.

steps.text: Heat stroke is the most serious kind: confusion, slurred speech, passing out, a seizure, or very hot skin. It can kill, so get emergency help.
steps.quote: Heat stroke is the most serious heat-related illness

steps.text: Move them to shade or somewhere cool and take off outer clothing.
steps.quote: Move the worker to a shaded, cool area and remove outer clothing

steps.text: Cool them fast: wet their skin, put cold wet cloths on the head, neck, armpits and groin, soak their clothes with cool water, and fan them.
steps.quote: Place cold wet cloths or ice on the head, neck, armpits, and groin

steps.text: Stay with them until help comes.
steps.quote: Stay with the worker until emergency medical services arrive

steps.text: Heat exhaustion (headache, nausea, dizziness, weakness, heavy sweating, thirst): get out of the heat, take off extra clothing, and take frequent sips of cool water.
steps.quote: Encourage frequent sips of cool water

guides.title: Hypothermia: too cold
guides.summary: Shivering, confused, fumbling or very sleepy from the cold.

steps.text: Warning signs: shivering, exhaustion, confusion, fumbling hands, memory loss, slurred speech, or drowsiness. Someone with hypothermia may not notice it themselves.
steps.quote: a person may not know that it's happening and won't be able to do anything about it

steps.text: It can happen above 40°F (4°C) too, if you're wet from rain, sweat or cold water.
steps.quote: it can occur even at cool temperatures (above 40°F) if a person becomes chilled from rain, sweat, or submersion in cold water

steps.text: Get them into shelter, out of the wind, and take off wet clothing.
steps.quote: Remove any wet clothing the person is wearing

steps.text: Warm the middle of the body first: chest, neck, head and groin. Skin-to-skin contact under loose, dry blankets or clothes works.
steps.quote: You can also use skin-to-skin contact under loose, dry layers of blankets, clothing, towels, or sheets

steps.text: Warm drinks can help if they're awake. No alcohol, and nothing to drink if they're unconscious.
steps.quote: Warm drinks can help increase body temperature, but do not give alcoholic drinks

steps.text: Once they're warmer, keep them dry and wrapped up, including the head and neck.
steps.quote: After body temperature has increased, keep the person dry and wrap their body

guides.title: Frostbite
guides.summary: Fingers, toes, ears or nose numb, white, grey or hard from cold.

steps.text: Check for hypothermia first and treat that before the frostbite.
steps.quote: Check for hypothermia and treat those symptoms first

steps.text: Get out of the cold. Take off wet clothes and tight rings or jewelry.
steps.quote: Remove any tight jewelry and wet clothes

steps.text: Don't thaw it if it might freeze again. Refreezing does more damage, so wait until you're somewhere you can stay warm.
steps.quote: Refreezing of thawed extremities can cause more severe damage

steps.text: If help is far away, soak the area in warm (never hot) water, about 104 to 108°F (40 to 42°C), for 15 to 30 minutes. It may burn and swell as it warms.
steps.quote: The recommended water temperature is 104°F to 108°F (40°C to 42.2°C)

steps.text: Don't rub it, and don't warm it with a fire, heater or hair dryer. The skin can burn without you feeling it.
steps.quote: Direct heat can burn the tissues that are already damaged

steps.text: Afterward, cover it with dry dressings, keep frostbitten fingers or toes apart, and move them as little as you can.
steps.quote: Move thawed areas as little as possible

guides.title: Spider bites, ticks and stings
guides.summary: A spider bite, a tick stuck in the skin, or a bee or wasp sting.

steps.text: Spider bite: stay calm, wash it with soap and water, and put a cold, wet cloth on it. Raise it if you can.
steps.quote: Apply a cloth dampened with cold water or filled with ice to the bite area to reduce swelling

steps.text: Spider bite: don't try to get the venom out. Get medical help, and if it's safe, note what the spider looked like.
steps.quote: Do not attempt to remove venom

steps.text: Tick: take it off as soon as you can. With fine tweezers or your fingers, grip it as close to the skin as you can.
steps.quote: Grasp the tick as close to the skin's surface as possible using clean fine-tipped tweezers

steps.text: Tick: pull straight out with steady pressure. Don't twist or jerk it, and don't crush it with your fingers.
steps.quote: Pull tick away from the skin with steady, even pressure

steps.text: Tick: clean the bite and your hands afterward, and check for more ticks. If a rash or fever comes in the days or weeks after, see a doctor.
steps.quote: If you develop a rash or fever within several days to weeks after removing a tick, see your doctor

steps.text: Bee sting: scrape the stinger off with a fingernail or card. Don't squeeze it with tweezers.
steps.quote: scrape the stinger off the skin with something firm

steps.text: If swelling spreads to the face or throat, or breathing gets hard after any bite or sting, treat it as a severe allergic reaction.
steps.quote: A warning sign of dangerous throat swelling is a very hoarse or whispered voice

guides.title: Earthquake
guides.summary: The ground is shaking, or just stopped.

steps.text: Drop onto your hands and knees where you are.
steps.quote: Drop where you are onto hands and knees

steps.text: Cover your head and neck with your arm, under a sturdy table or next to an inside wall, away from windows.
steps.quote: If no shelter is nearby, crawl next to an interior wall (away from windows)

steps.text: Hold on until the shaking stops.
steps.quote: Hold until the shaking stops

steps.text: If you're inside during the shaking, stay inside and away from doorways.
steps.quote: If you are inside, stay and do not run outside; avoid doorways

steps.text: If you're outside, move to an open area away from buildings, trees, streetlights and power lines.
steps.quote: Move to an open area away from buildings, trees, streetlights and power lines

steps.text: If you're driving, pull over, stop and set the parking brake.
steps.quote: If you are in a car, pull over and stop. Set your parking brake

steps.text: Expect aftershocks, and drop, cover and hold on each time.
steps.quote: Expect aftershocks to follow the main shock of an earthquake

steps.text: After the shaking, if the building is damaged, get out and away from it.
steps.quote: If you are in a damaged building, go outside and quickly move away from the building

steps.text: If you're trapped, text or bang on a pipe or wall instead of shouting.
steps.quote: If you are trapped, send a text or bang on a pipe or wall

steps.text: If you're near the coast, go inland or to high ground as soon as the shaking stops.
steps.quote: go inland or to higher ground immediately after the shaking stops

guides.title: Tsunami
guides.summary: A tsunami warning, or the sea suddenly rising or draining away.

steps.text: Signs of a tsunami: an earthquake, a loud roar from the sea, or the sea suddenly rising or draining away.
steps.quote: a loud roar from the ocean

steps.text: If you see a sign or hear a warning, leave right away.
steps.quote: Leave as soon as you see any natural signs of a tsunami or receive an official tsunami warning

steps.text: Go to high ground at least 100 feet (30 m) above sea level, or at least a mile (1.6 km) inland.
steps.quote: Pick shelters 100 feet or more above sea level, or at least one mile inland

steps.text: If you feel an earthquake, protect yourself from the shaking first, then go.
steps.quote: protect yourself from the earthquake first

steps.text: If you're on a boat, head out to sea.
steps.quote: If you are in a boat, go out to sea

guides.title: Avalanche
guides.summary: Someone is caught or buried in an avalanche, or the slope looks unstable.

steps.text: Stay off slopes steeper than about 30 degrees, and out from under them.
steps.quote: Avoid areas of increased risk, such as slopes steeper than 30 degrees or areas under steep slopes

steps.text: If someone is buried, call for help, then search only if it's safe for you.
steps.quote: call 9-1-1 and then begin to search if it is safe to do so

steps.text: Act fast: once an avalanche stops, the snow sets hard and buried people can't dig out.
steps.quote: When an avalanche stops, the snow becomes solid like concrete and people are unable to dig out

steps.text: Once someone is out, warm the middle of their body first and keep them dry.
steps.quote: Warm the center of the body first

guides.title: Hurricane or typhoon
guides.summary: A hurricane or big tropical storm is coming or has hit.

steps.text: If officials tell you to evacuate, go right away.
steps.quote: If you live in a mandatory evacuation zone and local officials tell you to evacuate, do so immediately

steps.text: For high winds, shelter in a storm shelter or an inside room.
steps.quote: Take refuge in a designated storm shelter or an interior room for high winds

steps.text: If flooding traps you, go to the highest floor, but not into a closed attic.
steps.quote: Do not climb into a closed attic

steps.text: Don't walk, swim or drive through flood water.
steps.quote: Do not walk, swim or drive through flood waters

steps.text: After the storm, stay out of flood water: downed power lines can charge it.
steps.quote: Underground or downed power lines can electrically charge the water

steps.text: Use texts instead of calls, and save calls for emergencies.
steps.quote: Save phone calls for emergencies

guides.title: Landslide or mudslide
guides.summary: Rock, mud or debris sliding down a slope, or signs one is coming.

steps.text: If you're in the path of a landslide, move uphill as fast as you can.
steps.quote: If you do get stuck in the path of a landslide move uphill as quickly as possible

steps.text: Never cross a road with water or mud flowing over it.
steps.quote: Never cross a road with water or mud flowing

steps.text: When slides are likely, stay out of river valleys and low ground.
steps.quote: Avoid river valleys and low-lying areas during times of danger

steps.text: If a stream suddenly turns muddy, a landslide may be coming.
steps.quote: water that changes from clear to muddy

steps.text: During heavy storms, stay awake: many landslide deaths happen while people sleep.
steps.quote: Many deaths from landslides occur while people are sleeping

steps.text: After a slide, stay away from the slide area.
steps.quote: Stay away from the slide area

guides.title: Volcano and ash
guides.summary: A volcano is erupting, or ash is falling.

steps.text: If you're told to evacuate, go early.
steps.quote: If advised to evacuate, do so early

steps.text: Stay away from areas downwind of the volcano and valleys downstream of it.
steps.quote: Avoid areas downwind and river valleys downstream of the volcano

steps.text: If ash is falling, stay inside and seal doors, windows and vents.
steps.quote: Cover ventilation openings and seal doors and windows

steps.text: If you must go outside in ash, cover your nose and mouth with a dust mask or cloth.
steps.quote: use a dust mask or cloth mask as a last resort if you must be outside

steps.text: If you must drive in ash, keep the windows up and the air conditioning off.
steps.quote: If you must drive, keep the windows up and do not use the air conditioning system

guides.title: Winter storm or blizzard
guides.summary: Heavy snow, ice or a blizzard, at home or on the road.

steps.text: If a winter storm warning is out, get to shelter right away.
steps.quote: IF YOU ARE UNDER A WINTER STORM WARNING, FIND SHELTER RIGHT AWAY

steps.text: If you're stuck in your car, stay inside it.
steps.quote: If trapped in your car, then stay inside

steps.text: Run generators and grills only outdoors, away from windows.
steps.quote: Only use generators and grills outdoors and away from windows

steps.text: If you must go outside, wear layers of warm clothing.
steps.quote: If you need to go outside, wear layers of warm clothing

steps.text: Don't overdo it shoveling or walking in deep snow.
steps.quote: avoiding overexertion when shoveling snow and walking in the snow

steps.text: Frostbite signs: numbness, and white, grayish-yellow, firm or waxy skin.
steps.quote: Signs: Numbness, white or grayish-yellow skin, firm or waxy skin

guides.title: Caught in a rip current
guides.summary: Being pulled out to sea by a current at the beach.

steps.text: Stay calm: a rip current pulls you out, not under.
steps.quote: Rip currents don't pull you under

steps.text: Don't swim straight back against the current; it will wear you out.
steps.quote: Trying to swim against a rip current will only use up your energy

steps.text: Swim along the shoreline until you're out of the pull, then angle back to shore.
steps.quote: Swim along the shoreline until you escape the current's pull

steps.text: If you can't reach shore, float, face the shore, and call or wave for help.
steps.quote: If you feel you can't reach shore, relax, face the shore, and call or wave for help

guides.title: Fell through ice
guides.summary: You (or someone) broke through ice into the water.

steps.text: If you fall through, keep your winter clothes on: they trap air and help you float.
steps.quote: Heavy clothes won't drag you down, but instead can trap air to provide warmth and flotation

steps.text: Turn back toward the way you came.
steps.quote: Turn toward the direction you came

steps.text: Put your arms on the solid ice, kick your feet, and work your way forward onto it.
steps.quote: Kick your feet and dig in your ice picks to work your way back onto the solid ice

steps.text: Once you're out, lie flat and roll away from the hole.
steps.quote: Lie flat on the ice once you are out and roll away from the hole

steps.text: Then get somewhere warm, dry and sheltered, and warm up right away.
steps.quote: Get to a warm, dry, sheltered area and re-warm yourself immediately

guides.title: Someone is in the water
guides.summary: Someone has fallen through ice, or is struggling in the water, and you want to help.

steps.text: Call for help first, and don't run to the edge.
steps.quote: Resist the urge to run up to the edge of the hole

steps.text: Shout to them and keep encouraging them.
steps.quote: Shout to the victim to encourage them to fight to survive

steps.text: From a safe spot, hold out a rope, branch or ladder; if they start pulling you in, let go.
steps.quote: If the person starts to pull you in, release your grip on the object and start over

steps.text: Throw them a rope or something that floats.
steps.quote: Toss one end of a rope or something that will float to the victim

steps.text: Don't go out to them yourself unless nothing else is possible.
steps.quote: A non-professional shouldn't go out on the ice to perform a rescue unless all other basic rescue techniques have been ruled out

steps.text: Cold water makes people gasp, so even strong swimmers can drown in it.
steps.quote: The sudden gasp and rapid breathing alone creates a greater risk of drowning, even for confident swimmers in calm waters

guides.title: House fire
guides.summary: Fire or smoke in a building you're in.

steps.text: Get low and crawl under the smoke to your way out.
steps.quote: Drop down to the floor and crawl low, under any smoke to your exit

steps.text: If a door or its handle is hot, or smoke comes around it, keep it shut and use another way out.
steps.quote: If either is hot, or if there is smoke coming around the door, leave the door closed and use your second way out

steps.text: Open doors slowly.
steps.quote: If you open a door, open it slowly

steps.text: If you can't reach someone, get out and tell the emergency operator where they are.
steps.quote: Tell the emergency operator where the person is located

steps.text: If you can't get out, signal at a window with a light-colored cloth or a flashlight.
steps.quote: signal for help at the window with a light-colored cloth or a flashlight

steps.text: If your clothes catch fire, stop, drop, cover your face and roll until the fire is out.
steps.quote: Roll over and over or back and forth until the fire is out

guides.title: Carbon monoxide
guides.summary: A CO alarm is going off, or headache and dizziness near a heater, stove, generator or engine.
keywords: everyone in our house has a headache

steps.text: If a CO alarm goes off, don't look for the cause. Go outside into fresh air right away.
steps.quote: Immediately move outside to fresh air

steps.text: Do the same if you have a headache, dizziness, weakness, sick stomach or confusion near something that burns fuel. CO has no smell or color.
steps.quote: If you think you are experiencing any of the symptoms of CO poisoning, get outside to fresh air immediately

steps.text: Call for help from outside. Don't go back in. People can pass out and die if they stay.
steps.quote: You could lose consciousness and die if you stay in the home

steps.text: Never run a generator inside a home, garage, tent or cabin, even with doors and windows open.
steps.quote: Never use a generator inside your home or garage, even if doors and windows are open

steps.text: Never burn charcoal or use a camp stove or fuel heater indoors or in a tent.
steps.quote: Never use a portable gas camp stove indoors

steps.text: Never heat a home with a gas oven or stove.
steps.quote: Never heat your house with a gas oven

guides.title: Gas leak
guides.summary: A smell of gas (rotten eggs) at home or near a pipeline.

steps.text: If you smell gas, stop what you're doing and leave right away.
steps.quote: If you smell gas, stop what you are doing and leave the area immediately

steps.text: On the way out, don't touch light switches, phones or garage door openers.
steps.quote: That includes light switches, telephones/cell phones, or garage door openers

steps.text: Once you're safely away, call the gas company or emergency services.
steps.quote: Once you are in a safe location, call your utility company or 911

guides.title: Power outage
guides.summary: The power is out, maybe for a long time.

steps.text: Keep the fridge and freezer closed.
steps.quote: Keep freezers and refrigerators closed

steps.text: Run a generator only outdoors, at least 20 feet (6 m) from windows.
steps.quote: Generators, camp stoves or charcoal grills should always be used outdoors and at least 20 feet away from windows

steps.text: Don't heat your home with a gas stove or oven.
steps.quote: Do not use a gas stove or oven to heat your home

steps.text: Unplug appliances and electronics to protect them from a power surge.
steps.quote: Disconnect appliances and electronics to avoid damage from electrical surges

steps.text: If it's dangerously hot or cold, go to a place in town that has power.
steps.quote: Go to a community location with power if heat or cold is extreme

steps.text: If medicines need a fridge or a device needs power, make a backup plan early.
steps.quote: Have alternate plans for refrigerating medicines or using power-dependent medical devices

guides.title: Chemical spill or toxic gas
guides.summary: A chemical leak, toxic smoke or a 'shelter in place' order.

steps.text: Some toxic chemicals have no smell. Trouble breathing or stinging eyes can be a sign.
steps.quote: Remember that some toxic chemicals are odorless

steps.text: If you're outside, get away fast, upwind of the source.
steps.quote: Move away immediately, in a direction upwind of the source

steps.text: If you're told to evacuate, go right away.
steps.quote: If asked to evacuate, do so immediately

steps.text: If you're told to stay inside, turn off air conditioning, fans and vents.
steps.quote: Turn off air conditioners and ventilation systems

steps.text: If you're staying inside, seal gaps around doors and windows with wet towels, plastic or tape.
steps.quote: Seal gaps under and around the following areas with wet towels, plastic sheeting, duct tape, wax paper or aluminum foil

steps.text: If fumes may have got in, take shallow breaths through a cloth.
steps.quote: Take shallow breaths through a cloth or a towel if gas or vapors could have entered the building

steps.text: Don't eat or drink anything that may be contaminated.
steps.quote: Avoid eating or drinking any food or water that may be contaminated

guides.title: Boat trouble on open water
guides.summary: Out of fuel, broken down, leaking, swamped or capsized at sea or on a lake.

steps.text: Get everyone into a lifejacket now.
steps.quote: Make sure everyone is wearing a lifejacket.

steps.text: If you have a marine radio, make a distress call on VHF channel 16.
steps.quote: make a distress call using your marine radio on channel 16 for VHF

steps.text: If your radio isn't working, use a phone if you have any signal.
steps.quote: Use your marine radio, if it's working, to make a distress call.

steps.text: When you reach anyone, tell them what's wrong and where you are.
steps.quote: contact authorities and surrounding vessels to advise your situation and your position

steps.text: If you have an EPIRB or distress beacon, switch it on and leave it on until rescuers tell you to turn it off.
steps.quote: Switch on the EPIRB and leave it on until emergency services tell you to turn it off.

steps.text: If water is coming in, bail or pump it out.
steps.quote: Start pumps or have someone start bailing.

steps.text: Find where the water is coming in, and try to stop or slow the leak.
steps.quote: Take steps to stop or slow down the leak.

steps.text: Stay with your boat, even if it capsizes: it's easier for rescuers to find.
steps.quote: Stay with your capsized vessel - this makes it easier for rescuers to find you.

steps.text: Don't try to swim to shore unless it's very close and there's a safe place to land.
steps.quote: Do not try to swim ashore unless it is very close and a suitable landing place exists.

steps.text: Make yourself as easy to see as you can for boats and aircraft.
steps.quote: Make yourself as visible as you can to both ships and aircraft.

steps.text: If you have flares, save them until you can see an aircraft or another boat.
steps.quote: Always delay using flares until you can see an aircraft, or until people on shore or in other boats are in visual range.

steps.text: If you're in the water, keep your lifejacket on and huddle together.
steps.quote: Do not remove your lifejacket and, if you are in the water, stay together in a HUDDLE or HELP position.

steps.text: Put on more clothes if you can, to help keep warm.
steps.quote: Put on more clothes if you can - this helps keep you warm and may delay or prevent hypothermia.

guides.title: Crisis lines outside the US
guides.summary: Mental-health crisis lines by country, used only in the crisis notice.

steps.text: Australia crisis line: call Lifeline on 13 11 14, any time.
steps.quote: You can also call Lifeline on 13 11 14 - 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

steps.text: UK crisis line: call Samaritans on 116 123.
steps.quote: call 116 123 to talk to Samaritans

steps.text: New Zealand crisis line: text 1737, or call 0800 1737 1737, to talk to a counsellor.
steps.quote: 1737 is staffed by a team of paid counsellors who can talk to you if you have mental health or addiction problems

outOfScope.sources: Warning signs added 2026-11-07 from official pages (CDC, NIH, NIMH, Ready.gov), each quote verified: ai-experiments/medical-signs.json
outOfScope.message: If there is any way to reach 911, do that now. Tenvia's first-aid steps are a draft and don't replace medical help.
I am so sorry you are carrying this. You matter. Please reach out to someone now: call or text 988 in the US, or 911.
